stories.body: Israel's election produced no clear governing majority, with exit polls putting Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc and the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot roughly tied in the 120-seat Knesset. Netanyahu's Likud appears set to remain the largest single party, while final results will be affected by absentee ballots and coalition talks that could take weeks. The unusually high turnout followed a campaign shaped by the October 7 attack and its aftermath, and the strong showing by Arab parties may prove decisive in determining whether either bloc can reach 61 seats.
stories.headline: Israeli election ends in deadlock as Netanyahu and Eisenkot seek to form a government

stories.body: Arab-led parties in Israel are projected to win about 18 or 19 Knesset seats, their strongest result, after turnout in Palestinian-Israeli communities reportedly approached 80 percent. The gains could make the Joint List and Ra'am pivotal in a deadlocked parliament, but Eisenkot's opposition bloc faces a difficult choice after campaigning against reliance on Arab parties. Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas has indicated openness to preventing another Netanyahu-led government, while negotiations with the larger Joint List could be more contentious.
stories.headline: Arab parties make major gains in Israel's election amid record turnout

stories.body: Human rights groups have urged governments to reject UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh's candidacy to become the next UN secretary-general, citing allegations that the United Arab Emirates has supported Sudan's Rapid Support Forces. Abu Dhabi denies those accusations. Nusseibeh, 48, is seeking to become the first woman to lead the United Nations.
stories.headline: Rights groups oppose UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh's bid for UN secretary-general

stories.body: King Charles III began a nine-day Caribbean tour in the Bahamas by acknowledging the "great suffering of the past," amid renewed calls for Britain to apologize and engage in reparations talks over transatlantic slavery. He will also visit Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda, where he is due to attend a Commonwealth summit at which the legacy of slavery will be discussed. Caribbean reparations advocates welcomed recognition of the history but said his remarks fell short of a formal apology or a commitment to remedy enduring harm.
stories.headline: King Charles begins Caribbean tour acknowledging slavery's legacy

stories.body: Africa's Ebola outbreak has passed 10,000 cases, health authorities said, with the overwhelming majority of infections reported in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The outbreak is being driven by the rare Bundibugyo species of Ebola, for which there are currently no approved vaccines.
stories.headline: Ebola outbreak in Africa surpasses 10,000 cases, concentrated in DR Congo

stories.body: A student-backed opposition list of academics, engineers, artists and activists has defeated President Aleksandar Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party after nearly two years of anti-corruption protests. The result ends 14 years of SNS dominance, but analysts expect a new government to focus first on rebuilding institutions, the judiciary, police and media rather than rapidly changing foreign policy. Relations with neighboring states and Serbia's path toward the European Union are likely to remain difficult during a potentially turbulent transition.
stories.headline: Serbia's student-led opposition movement defeats Vucic's ruling party

stories.body: Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro has reportedly arrived in the United States after Brazil's Supreme Court ordered him to surrender his passports in a money-laundering investigation. Bolsonaro has not been charged and denies wrongdoing, but missed the deadline to turn over the documents. A senior US State Department official said the Trump administration would issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family, prompting criticism from Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and US Democrats seeking answers about whether Washington assisted his departure.
stories.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro flees Brazil after presidential defeat as US says it will grant him a visa

stories.body: Republicans' online small-donor base has shrunk while Democrats' has grown, increasing the GOP's reliance on Donald Trump and a relatively small group of wealthy donors. Analysis of federal filings found about 1.5 million WinRed donors this cycle, down from 2.2 million at the comparable point in 2022, while ActBlue donors rose to roughly 6.6 million. More than three in five WinRed donors have given to Trump-related groups despite his not being on the ballot, leaving Republican candidates at a fundraising disadvantage and limiting their ability to buy advertising at candidate rates.
stories.headline: Republicans grow more dependent on Trump and megadonors as their online small-donor base contracts

stories.body: House Democrats have added nine candidates to their Red to Blue program since September, extending their target map into more Republican-leaning districts as national conditions appear favorable. But recent history suggests the late additions are long shots: since 2018, no Democrat added to the program in September or October has flipped a Republican-held seat. The designations can still attract money and signal momentum, though most of the newly elevated candidates trail their Republican opponents financially.
stories.headline: Democrats expand House targets into increasingly Republican territory in the final campaign stretch

stories.body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio appeared with President Donald Trump at a Texas rally centered on Venezuelan oil, giving Republicans a glimpse of the campaign role many want him to take before the midterms. Rubio has largely avoided overt political events in keeping with State Department tradition, and the administration said he attended in his capacity as national security adviser. Republican strategists nonetheless see him as a potentially effective surrogate, particularly with centrist and Hispanic voters, as the party faces a difficult campaign environment.
stories.headline: Marco Rubio joins Trump at a Texas rally as Republicans press for a larger campaign role

stories.body: The European Commission has opened an examination of whether Spain complied with EU law when it approved an extraordinary migrant regularization program by decree. The review follows a complaint by the Catalan separatist party Junts, which argues that the measure should have been passed through parliament and may conflict with EU rules on returns, asylum and notification of migration measures. Spain received nearly 1.2 million applications under the program, well above the government's initial estimate of about 500,000.
stories.headline: European Commission examines Spain's migrant regularization plan

stories.body: Representatives of major National Police unions and Civil Guard associations began an indefinite sit-in at Spain's Interior Ministry after negotiations over retirement conditions collapsed. The groups are demanding recognition as high-risk professions and retirement terms comparable to those available to regional and local police. Sixteen representatives began the protest, which police later dispersed, after the government said the calling of a general election ended the negotiating process.
stories.headline: Spain's police and Civil Guard unions begin an indefinite sit-in over retirement conditions

stories.body: Spain's conservative Popular Party and the far-right Vox have agreed to coordinate for the Senate election in an unprecedented arrangement that includes PP lists carrying candidates closely linked to Vox. The PP will also not field Senate candidates in Lleida, Tarragona and Gipuzkoa, arguing that polls give it no realistic prospect of winning seats there. PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo defended the decision as a tactical choice, while the deal underscores Vox's influence over the coalition's electoral strategy.
stories.headline: Spain's PP and Vox strike an unusual Senate-election pact

stories.body: Doctors in Catalonia's public and publicly contracted health system began an indefinite strike, led by the Metges de Catalunya union, over working hours, workloads and pay. The union seeks to end 24-hour shifts, move toward a 12-hour maximum working day, limit primary-care schedules and raise pay by at least 20 percent. Hospitals must maintain extensive minimum services, including emergency and critical care, while primary-care centers are required to operate with at least 25 percent of staff on the first day of the strike.
stories.headline: Catalan doctors launch an indefinite strike over workloads, hours and pay

stories.body: Catalonia's government and Renfe have signed a long-awaited contract setting the financial and operating terms for Rodalies commuter rail and regional services through 2028. The agreement provides €1.408 billion over three years, funded by the Spanish state, including compensation for delays and costs associated with service disruptions after the Gelida accident. It also provides for 110 additional trains and a new joint monitoring commission, while Catalonia hopes a planned mixed public company will take over the next contract from 2029.
stories.headline: Catalonia and Renfe sign a €1.4 billion Rodalies and regional-rail contract through 2028

stories.body: Catalonia's unemployment rate rose to 8.3 percent in the third quarter, from 7.9 percent in the previous quarter, leaving 361,800 people unemployed, according to Spain's labor force survey. Employment increased by only 2,100 people, the weakest quarterly growth since 2019, while the active population grew by 20,900. Services added jobs, but industry and construction recorded substantial losses, signaling a slowdown in the labor market's post-pandemic improvement.
stories.headline: Catalan unemployment rises above 8% as job creation stalls
